_meta.description: Few-Shot Success Library — Vector DB Guardrail (Guardrail 1)
_meta.rationale: Stores proven successes as few-shot examples. When generating new content, the agent queries this library for the top matching past workflows and uses them as structural templates.

golden_runs.description: Noah transforms from regular clothes to blue super-suit on mountain peak at sunset. Blue energy swirl effect.
golden_runs.prompt_template: {character_name} transforming into {hero_name} on a {location}. {energy_type} energy swirl, superhero suit reveal. Cinematic lighting.
golden_runs.negative_used: blurry, low quality, text, watermark, deformed, disfigured
golden_runs.visual_notes: Perfect character consistency between keyframes. Energy effect is cinematic without overpowering the subject.

golden_runs.description: Super Noah hovering at eye-level with Dr. Robotnik's cockpit. Arms crossed, serious expression.
golden_runs.prompt_template: {hero_name} hovering in a standoff with {villain_name}. Intense eye-contact, serious expression.
golden_runs.negative_used: blurry, low quality, text, watermark, deformed, disfigured
golden_runs.visual_notes: Strong dual-character consistency. Villain design held through interpolation.

golden_runs.description: Super Noah lands in park surrounded by cheering crowd. Holding a puppy, winking.
golden_runs.prompt_template: {hero_name} has landed in a {location}. A crowd of happy {crowd_type} are cheering around him. He is holding a rescued {animal}. Heroic victory pose.
golden_runs.negative_used: blurry, low quality, text, watermark, deformed, disfigured
golden_runs.visual_notes: Large crowd scene maintained consistency. Sunset lighting added cinematic warmth.

golden_runs.description: Henrio in ruins with ancient pillars. Pixel art retro style.
golden_runs.prompt_template: {character_name} in {environment}. Pixel art style, retro 16-bit aesthetic.
golden_runs.negative_used: blurry, low quality, text, watermark, deformed, disfigured
golden_runs.visual_notes: Retro crunch filter (neighbor scaling) essential for sharp pixel art edges.

learnings: Resolution 1024x576 is the sweet spot for 16:9 cinematic output on 16GB VRAM.
97 frames (8*12+1) is the maximum safe frame count for single-shot generation.
Sequential shot generation (one at a time) prevents VRAM crashes. NEVER run parallel shots.
The 2-pass sigma schedule (8-step pass1 + 3-step pass2) produces the sharpest output.
Character consistency is maintained by using high-fidelity anchor keyframes from Gemini/Grok.
Crossfade duration of 1.0s feels cinematic. 0.5s is too abrupt for slow narrative pacing.
CRF 10 with 10-bit color (yuv420p10le) is production quality without excessive file size.
The 'Retro Crunch' filter (scale=256:-1:flags=neighbor,scale=1024:-1:flags=neighbor) is ONLY for pixel art.
Always use absolute paths in FFmpeg concat demuxer lists to avoid nested path resolution errors.
CFG above 4.0 causes 'deep-frying' artifacts with the distilled LTX 2.3 model.

failure_modes.symptom: System crash / force reboot during generation
failure_modes.cause: Multiple shots queued simultaneously exhausted VRAM

failure_modes.symptom: FFmpeg TransitionError: Impossible to open nested path
failure_modes.cause: Relative paths in concat demuxer list files
failure_modes.fix: Use Path.resolve() for all temp dirs, list files, and output paths

failure_modes.symptom: Character drifts into wrong design (e.g., Mario instead of Henrio)
failure_modes.fix: Use strict character description in every prompt: (hair color, outfit, specific features)

failure_modes.cause: CFG too high or wrong sigma schedule
failure_modes.fix: Keep CFG <= 4.0 for distilled model. Use proven sigma schedules from envelopes.
